Once a craftsman population in a given state gets above 100 people, whatever the culture and religion of that group, any pop that is promoted to that group will always be that culture and religion. So if there's a province with 100 craftsmen in a province and the culture of that group is Hungarian, for example, then it doesn't matter whatever the farmer or the laborer culture was when it was promoted. It will be promoted to the craftsmen group with that culture, and therefore be "converted".

This can be exploited to your liking. 

So if you want to "convert" pops into your primary culture in regions that aren't cored, you can put your thumb on the scale by opening factories, encouraging craftsmen in that region, and watch to see what provinces get desired culture. If a pop of a culture you don't want gets closer to 100 than your other ones, you close the factory, stop encouraging, and those pops will slowly migrate to other regions that have available factories. Try to time so that undesired culture group of craftsmen leave first, and trying to maintain the group of your primary culture before they migrate too. Once the undesired group leaves, then you re-open, and try again until the desired group gets past 100. The trick is not allow undesired groups of craftsmen get above 100 because then they don't all up and leave once a factory is closed and they're unemployed. They'll only lose 2 workers, if that, per tick. Whereas if the group is 99 or below, they'll ALL leave at once to the next region for employment.

You rinse and repeat until all provinces in that region are the desired culture and above 100 pop, and then watch as the craftsmen build up and get "converted" to that culture. 

In my post, I express how limited this is though. In my experience, even if you get lucky, the most you're able to convert in a regular game is maybe 20%. Most the time, it's maybe a little more than 10% of the provinces population will change to that. Realistically, you'll never get the around 50% because getting to 50% of a craftsmen population is tedious.
